title: Lens Usage Concentration
dataSources: Lightroom photo exports (`lightroom:photo`), Flickr photo metadata (`flickr:photo`), ShutterCount body audits (`shuttercount:camera`), and F3 card tests (`f3:card`).
app: Adobe Lightroom exports, Flickr API metadata, ShutterCount camera audits, and F3 SD-card health checks sent to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=lightroom:photo lens_model=*
| stats count as photos by lens_model
| eventstats sum(photos) as total_photos
| eval usage_pct=round(100*photos/total_photos,1)
| sort - photos
description: Shows which lenses dominate your edited photo library and how concentrated your actual usage has become.
value: Gear decisions get sharper when you know whether a lens is a genuine workhorse or just shelf decoration.
implementation: Export EXIF lens metadata from Lightroom and chart the resulting share of edited frames by lens.
visualization: Pareto chart of photos by lens model with cumulative share.
grandmaExplanation: It tracks which lenses you really use most instead of which ones you only hoped you would use.
